title: Player heartbeat, major 1
description: What Displayarr reports about one wall, as facts rather than a verdict. The document Displayarr writes today has no schema key, and a heartbeat without one is 1.0. Wave 2 adds the schema key (1.1) when the heartbeat moves to an HTTP POST. The server reads reported_at and keeps the rest as it came; additive keys are allowed. Semantics are in .prawduct/artifacts/player-contract.md. Minor 2 (wave 4) adds the optional capabilities block and scene_id, which Programming needs once it chooses label modes, judges adequacy per wall and shows whether a scene reached each wall.

reported_at.description: The instant of the report, RFC 3339 with an offset. The server treats any other spelling of this key as an unreadable heartbeat. The pattern is what enforces the offset; 'format' alone is not checked by every validator.

manifest_schema.description: The major.minor of the manifest the Player has loaded, or null before it has adopted one.

announced_content_id.description: What the television last announced it is showing, in the set's own words.

label_surface_working.description: Null until the surface has been given a label, including on a Player with no surface.

last_error.description: The last thing that went wrong, in the words the journal got. Not cleared by a good pass.

capabilities.description: Minor 2 (wave 4). What this Player can do, observed rather than configured. Programming chooses the wall's label mode from label_modes and judges a work's adequacy against screen.

backend.description: frame: push to a Samsung Frame's own art store. framebuffer: composite and draw to a screen this process owns.

label_modes.description: The label modes this Player can do now. panel needs e-ink hardware; caption needs a Player version that sets captions.

manifest_majors.description: The manifest majors this Player reads, so the server can say which Players a major 2 cutover would leave on yesterday's wall.

scene_id.description: Minor 2 (wave 4). The scene the wall is showing, or null when it follows the schedule, so the UI can show which walls a scene has reached.
